# Play — Combination Lock

- SudokuPad: [Combination Lock on SudokuPad](https://sudokupad.)
- f-puzzles: [Combination Lock on f-puzzles](https://www.f-puzzles.com/?)

Both links carry the same f-puzzles JSON (lz-string compressed), including the solution, so SudokuPad can check your answer.
The sandwich sums and the killer cage are native f-puzzles constraints. f-puzzles has no lockout line, so each line is drawn as a
cosmetic slate line, with cosmetic squares turned 45° as diamonds. The apps won't enforce the lockout rule; the rules text covers it. I have not opened the links in a browser.
If the diamonds don't show, use `grid.svg` in this folder as the reference picture.

Lockout lines (diamond, inner cells..., diamond): r6c3–r5c3–r4c3–r3c4–r3c5–r3c6–r4c7–r5c7–r6c7; r6c3–r6c4–r6c5–r6c6–r6c7; r9c3–r9c4–r9c5–r9c6–r9c7; r6c3–r7c3–r8c3–r9c3; r6c7–r7c7–r8c7–r9c7.

Keyhole cage: r7c5 + r8c5 = 16.

Sandwich sums: row 6: 28, row 9: 22, column 1: 30, row 5: 23, row 1: 12, row 8: 28, column 6: 10.

Fallback: `puzzle.json` in this folder is the machine-readable source (constraints, solution).
